# Changelog

All notable changes to Compagnon are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
Detailed notes for each version are on the corresponding GitHub Release.

<!-- compagnon:begin — generated by `compagnon changelog --write` from the archived changes; edit outside this block -->
## [Unreleased]

### Added

- A **Read and approve a plan** guide for product owners and other non-developers.
- Six pages each profile asked for — an annotated example plan, approving a plan on GitHub or GitLab, starting from nothing, adopting Compagnon on an existing project, deploying it for a team, and contributing — and "Reviewing a plan" explains how to read a modified rule.
- Two chapters, "Decisions" and "Error codes and fixes", gather what was spread across Concepts and the FAQ.

### Changed

- The documentation now opens with a short **Start here** path — Compagnon in two minutes, your first change in Claude Code, and a glossary — and a **Choose your path** page for five profiles, including people who do not code and only approve plans. Nothing was removed: the details moved to later sections.
- The whole French documentation now speaks French — « modification », « compétence », « spécification », « déroulé », « demande de fusion » — with the English word only between parentheses where it appears on screen.
- The everyday pages of the documentation are written in plain language: technical terms are replaced by everyday words, or explained the first time with a link to the glossary.
- The French documentation uses French words instead of anglicisms — a « modification » rather than a « change », a « compétence » rather than a « skill ».
- The explore and onboard skills now suggest each next step in plain words — "say “plan this change”" — with the slash command as an optional shortcut.
- Compagnon's skills now suggest each next step in plain words — "say “implement it”" — with the slash command as an optional shortcut, so you can go through a change without learning the commands.
- The documentation asks one question — what will you do with Compagnon? — and gives each of four profiles a short path of at most three pages, including a new one for people who do not code but want Claude to build something for them. The site's home page now exists in French.
- The documentation is rewritten for every profile: shorter everyday pages that end with "Go further", each topic explained once, thirteen diagrams of how Compagnon works, a new look and the "Compagnon by Mairistem" logo.
- The Jira integration is put forward — from the home page, the README and the first pages, you learn that "Prepare a plan for PROJ-123" makes Claude read the ticket and cite it in the plan.
- `compagnon docs --print` leaves out the diagrams' drawings and keeps their captions, so a terminal or an AI reads the caption instead of SVG markup.

### Removed

- The "Discovering AI agents" profile; links to the former profile sections of Choose your path (`#i-am-discovering-ai-agents`…) now open the page at its top.
<!-- compagnon:end -->

## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- Six built-in experts — security, privacy, accessibility, performance, operations and migration — challenge the plan and review the code when the change's proposal ticks their domain, each with concrete knowledge (signals, pitfalls per language, references) served by `compagnon roles`.
- The proposal has a `## Domains` section listing the domains the change touches, or `None`; `compagnon validate` reports an unknown domain or a malformed section as an error and a missing section as a warning, which fails `compagnon validate --strict`: add the section, or `None`, to your active changes.
- A role's activation can be `on_domain`; `compagnon roles --json` returns each role's `steps`, `domains`, `activatedBy` and, for active roles, its `knowledge`, which `compagnon roles --knowledge` prints.
- Roles are configurable: `roles:` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` turns a review role on or off (`always` / `never`) and adds your own "done when" criteria; `roles:` in a change's `change.yaml` overrides the activation for that change.
- `compagnon roles` lists the roles active at a workflow step with their criteria, or every role with its activation; `compagnon instructions --json` returns the artifact's role in a `role` field.
- A schema artifact may declare its role as data (`role:` with id, name, question and "done when" criteria).
- `compagnon doctor` lists the active and disabled roles.
- `/compagnon-apply` reviews the code a change touched as a newcomer would, simplifies what is unambiguous without changing behavior, and reports up to three readability notes in its summary.
- Experts carry triggers — file paths, dependency manifests and code patterns — and `compagnon roles --change` reports the domains the change's diff suggests; `compagnon validate` warns (`domain_suggested`) when a suggested domain is neither ticked nor kept unticked with a reason on its line (`- [ ] security — reason`).
- A `triggers:` key in `_compagnon/config.yaml` adds the project's own sensitive paths and patterns. An earlier compagnon ignores it with an `unknown_config_key` warning, which fails its `compagnon validate --strict`: raise `compagnon_version` to this release when you add it.
- Isolated review. Set `review: { mode: isolated }` in `_compagnon/config.yaml`, or in a change's `change.yaml`, and `/compagnon-propose` and `/compagnon-apply` run each reviewing role as a separate sub-agent that sees only its role, the project's rules and the material — never the conversation — then merge their findings, crediting every role that raised one. The default stays `inline`. Run `compagnon update` after changing the mode.
- `compagnon roles --json` gives the review mode and measures the material the reviewers read, naming the files to summarize beyond a size limit; `compagnon review` shows how each step was reviewed, what was summarized and which roles fell back to inline.
- `compagnon doctor` reports skills generated for another review mode (`skills_review_mode`).
- A "Reliability of the roles" chapter shows how the built-in roles score on the evaluation suite — what they find, what they invent, and which fail their thresholds — generated from the committed baseline, in English and French.
- Each change keeps a review record, `review.md`, where the roles write their findings with a severity, a confidence, a location and the quoted evidence, and where every answer — fixed, disputed, accepted risk, deferred, rejected — is recorded with who decided it. `compagnon review` shows it and what is left to decide.
- `compagnon validate` checks the review record: its format, that each cited file and line exists and that the quoted evidence is really there.
- The built-in roles are measured by an evaluation suite in the repository: seeded defects and clean controls score what each role finds, misses and invents, and whether its evidence is real. The baseline is published in `evals/baseline/report.md`, and the Roles chapter explains it.
- Specs and deltas can be written with French structural keywords — `### Exigence :`, `#### Scénario :`, `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`, `DOIT` and the others — next to the English ones, which keep working.
- The keywords come from a per-language catalog, so a new language can be added with one file.
- `compagnon search <query>` finds the requirements and decisions that match a query, ranked by relevance, and `compagnon show <capability>::<requirement>` prints a single requirement.
- When you correct the agent on how your project does things during `/compagnon-propose`, `/compagnon-apply` or `/compagnon-update`, it notes the correction in the change's `corrections.md`, which `compagnon validate` checks and `compagnon review` lists, so that the instruction is not lost when the change is archived.
- `roles: { <role>: { model: opus | sonnet | haiku | inherit } }` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` sets the model a role's review runs on in the isolated review mode; no role sets one by default. A project that sets it should first raise `compagnon_version` to this release, since an older compagnon refuses the key — and a source shared through `inherits:` should not set it until every project inheriting from it runs this release.
- a model set on the `developer` role (`roles: { developer: { model: sonnet } }`) now runs the implementation of `/compagnon-apply` in a sub-agent on that model, while the session keeps the review; without a model nothing changes.
- `compagnon instructions --json` gives `keywordLanguage` and `keywords`, the language and the texts of the structural keywords to write; a project schema may hold one template set per language under `templates/<language>/`.
- `compagnon migrate` converts a project set up with codev — planning folder, lock file, configuration, skills, `CLAUDE.md` and CI workflow — and Compagnon tells you to run it when it finds a codev project.
- Compagnon has its own logo, in the documentation, the README and the site.

### Changed

- **BREAKING** The `analyst` role can no longer be disabled: remove `analyst: never` from `roles:` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` or a change's `change.yaml`.
- **BREAKING** `compagnon archive` refuses (`review_blocked`) a change whose review record is missing for a step where roles were active, or that still has a high-severity finding open or disputed. For a change started with an earlier compagnon, run the review again or turn its review roles off in its `change.yaml`; a team that does not use the skills turns `skeptic` and `newcomer` off in `_compagnon/config.yaml`.
- **BREAKING** A project whose `language:` is French now gets its planning artifacts written entirely in French, structural keywords included (`## Changements`, `### Exigence :`, `DOIT`). Every teammate and the CI need a compagnon that reads French keywords: raise `compagnon_version` to this release. Existing artifacts and specs keep their keywords. To keep English keywords, set `language: en`, which also writes the prose in English.
- **BREAKING** `compagnon validate`, `compagnon sync` and `compagnon archive` refuse to run when the running compagnon does not satisfy the project's `compagnon_version`; run `compagnon self-update`. Projects without `compagnon_version` are unaffected. With an upper bound (`^0.6`), widen `compagnon_version` before upgrading past it, or install the version `compagnon doctor` names. A CI job pinned with `COMPAGNON_VERSION=` needs its pin raised whenever `compagnon_version` is.
- **BREAKING** codev is now **Compagnon**. The command is `compagnon`, the planning folder is `_compagnon/`, the skills are `/compagnon-*`, the configuration key is `compagnon_version` and environment variables start with `COMPAGNON_`. Run `compagnon migrate` once in each existing project.
- **BREAKING** Release archives are named `compagnon-<version>-<target>`, the repository is `mairistem/compagnon` (installers and update check), the lock file is `_compagnon/compagnon.lock`, the generated CI workflow is `.github/workflows/compagnon.yml`, the update cache lives in a `compagnon` folder, and managed markers read `compagnon`. Scripts that download `codev-*` archives or read these paths must be updated; `compagnon migrate` handles the project files.
- **BREAKING** JSON error codes that contained `codev` are renamed (`no_codev_root` becomes `no_compagnon_root`, and so on).
- `/compagnon-propose` caps its Points to challenge at five across the skeptic and the experts, and `/compagnon-apply` ends with up to five Review notes (formerly Readability notes), each tagged with its role; a high-severity security or privacy finding is never dropped.
- `compagnon doctor` names the roles activated by domain.
- The default schema's instructions no longer start with a `Role:` prose block; the role comes in the `role` field of `compagnon instructions`, and `/compagnon-propose` and `/compagnon-apply` take their review criteria from `compagnon roles`.
- The architect's criteria of the default schema require the simplest approach that satisfies the specs, and a design a newcomer can follow without knowing its history.
- The `By stack` part of a role's knowledge keeps only the languages detected in the project; `compagnon roles --all-stacks` serves every language.
- `/compagnon-propose` ticks or justifies each suggested domain, and `/compagnon-apply` asks you to decide a suggested domain still unticked. Since `domain_suggested` is a warning, `compagnon validate --strict` fails until each suggestion is ticked or justified.
- The role evaluation suite has harder cases — subtle defects, two defects of different severity per expert, Python cases and more clean controls — and pairs a finding with a seeded defect only when they name the same category of issue. The committed baseline in `evals/baseline/report.md` is recorded again.
- A project or a change that sets `review:` needs this compagnon release or a later one everywhere it is read, CI included: an older compagnon warns about the unknown key (and fails with `--strict`), and refuses a `change.yaml` that sets it. Raise `compagnon_version` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` to this release when you set the mode.
- `/compagnon-propose` and `/compagnon-apply` write their findings into the review record, let the author answer each one and the reviewer re-check it, and ask you to decide what is still disputed.
- The reviewing roles report fewer false positives. A finding presented to you with high confidence now quotes the line and states the scenario that fails; hypotheses and preferences stay in the review record with low confidence. Each defect is reported once, and each expert says what lies outside its domain.
- The skeptic no longer reviews security, privacy, migration, operations, performance or accessibility itself: it challenges the plan's logic and evidence and checks that the proposal's Domains bring the experts who do. Run `compagnon update` to refresh your skills.
- The review steps of `/compagnon-propose` and `/compagnon-apply` take fewer turns and ask for fewer permissions: `compagnon roles --at` now lists the roles disabled at the step, and the skills read compagnon's output as printed instead of filtering it through other programs. Measured on the evaluation suite with no change in what the roles find: permission denials down 46 %, context re-read down 16 %, turns down 6 %, time down 12 %, cost down 7 %.
- once the proposal is written, `compagnon instructions` names the existing requirements the change likely touches, and `/compagnon-propose` reads and modifies them rather than adding new ones beside them.
- An unknown key in a change's `change.yaml`, a project `schema.yaml`, a role's settings in `_compagnon/config.yaml` or an ADR frontmatter is now ignored with a warning naming it and pointing to `compagnon self-update`, instead of failing; `compagnon validate --strict` still fails on it. A file written for a newer compagnon no longer stops an older one.
- `compagnon decision accept` keeps the frontmatter fields it does not know when it rewrites an ADR.
- Existing CI jobs that install codev with `CODEV_VERSION` keep installing codev; switch them to `COMPAGNON_VERSION` and `compagnon` when you migrate. GitLab jobs and hand-edited workflows are not changed by `compagnon migrate`.
- A codev 0.6 binary can still `self-update` during the 0.7 series; it then tells you to rename it to `compagnon`.

### Fixed

- Archiving a change that modifies a spec's last requirement and adds requirements no longer cuts that requirement in two: the added ones are written after it.
- `compagnon update` refreshes the skills it rendered itself even when their version stamp has not changed, and preserves only the skills edited by hand; each skill now carries a checksum of its content. Skills generated by an earlier compagnon are rewritten on upgrade as before; on a build from source, skills of the same version without a checksum are still preserved, and one `compagnon update --force` brings them under the checksum — check `git diff` first, since it also overwrites real hand edits.
- Earlier compagnon versions could cut a spec's last requirement in two when one change both modified it and added requirements; `compagnon validate` does not detect it, and syncing again does not repair it. If you archived such a change, look at the spec it modified (the diff of the archive) and repair it by hand or with a new `MODIFIED` delta.

## [0.6.1] - 2026-10-12

### Fixed

- `compagnon validate` no longer fails when `_compagnon/specs/` holds a Markdown file other than `spec.md`, and `compagnon list --specs` no longer shows such a file as a capability.
- A change created with a project schema whose `name:` differs from its folder can now be used; `compagnon schemas` warns about the mismatch with `schema_name_mismatch`.
- `archive` is refused as a change name, by `compagnon new change` and by `--change`, instead of being treated as a change.
- A failed `compagnon instructions --json` now carries `language`, like a successful one.
- Paths in JSON output use `/` separators on Windows too, as documented.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- `compagnon self-update` downloads the latest release for your platform, verifies its SHA-256, replaces the binary and refreshes the current project; `--check` only reports, `--snooze` silences the notice for 7 days, and a cargo or package-manager installation is left alone with the right command printed instead.
- `compagnon status` tells you when a newer Compagnon is available — at most one anonymous request to GitHub per day, never in CI or with `COMPAGNON_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` — and `compagnon status --json` exposes it in an `update` object; the skills offer to update at the start of an action.
- `compagnon_version` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` sets the Compagnon versions a team accepts; `compagnon doctor` reports a `compagnon_version` check when the running Compagnon does not satisfy it, or when a newer release is known.

### Changed

- A key of `_compagnon/config.yaml` that your Compagnon does not know — typically one added by a newer Compagnon — is now a warning `unknown_config_key` instead of an error, naming the key and the project's `compagnon_version`, and pointing to `compagnon self-update`; `compagnon validate --strict` and the new `config.keys` check of `compagnon doctor` report it. Compagnon 0.5 and earlier still reject such keys.

### Fixed

- When the running Compagnon is newer than the project's `compagnon_version` allows, `compagnon doctor` now suggests `compagnon self-update --version <X.Y.Z>` with a version that satisfies it, instead of a `compagnon self-update` that refuses to downgrade.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-10-12

### Changed

- **BREAKING:** `compagnon decision supersede`, `compagnon decision deviate` and
  `compagnon decision promote` now create a `proposed` decision, unsealed, like
  `compagnon decision new`: write or rework it, then run `compagnon decision accept
  <ID>` to make it take effect. Scripts that relied on these commands taking
  effect at once must add that step.
- `compagnon decision supersede` no longer modifies the old decision: it stays
  `accepted`, and in effect, until the new one is accepted. It now refuses a
  decision that is not `accepted` (`predecessor_not_accepted`).
- A deviation created by `compagnon decision deviate` only sets the inherited
  decision aside once it is accepted.
- `compagnon decision deviate --json` and `compagnon decision promote --json` no
  longer return `bodySha256`, since nothing is sealed.

### Added

- `compagnon decision accept` marks the decisions listed in `supersedes` as
  `superseded` in the same step, leaving their body and seal untouched, and
  lists them in a new `superseded` field of its JSON output. It refuses a
  predecessor that is no longer `accepted` — for example, one another decision
  superseded in the meantime — with `predecessor_not_accepted`.
- Each artifact instruction of the `spec-driven` schema opens with an explicit
  role and its "Done when" criteria: product owner (proposal), QA analyst
  (specs), architect (design), tech lead (tasks).
- `/compagnon-propose` checks traceability between capabilities, spec files,
  scenarios and task verifications before presenting the plan, and fixes the
  gaps in the artifacts.
- `/compagnon-propose` then challenges the plan as a skeptical reviewer — need,
  scope, specs, decisions, assumptions, tasks, plus security, compatibility,
  operability, performance or accessibility lenses when the proposal's Impact
  touches them, and the project's `rules:` — and ends its summary with at most
  five "Points to challenge", or says none was found.
- `compagnon init --inherit <SOURCE>` (repeatable) declares inherited sources in
  the generated `config.yaml` — a git URL with an optional `@<ref>` (`main` by
  default) or a local folder — and pins the git ones in `_compagnon/compagnon.lock`
  right away. A pinning failure only warns (`inherit_pin_failed`); an invalid
  value is refused before anything is written (`invalid_inherit`).
- `compagnon init` integrates Compagnon into the repository: a Compagnon section in
  `CLAUDE.md` telling Claude Code to plan behavior changes with
  `/compagnon-propose`, and on GitHub a `.github/workflows/compagnon.yml` running
  `compagnon validate --strict` with Compagnon pinned to the running version, and a
  Compagnon section in the pull request template. On GitLab it prints a job to
  paste. Opt out with `--no-claude-md`, `--no-ci`, `--no-pr-template` or
  `--no-integration`. Compagnon's text sits between `<!-- compagnon:begin -->` and
  `<!-- compagnon:end -->` markers and never replaces yours.
- `compagnon update` refreshes those managed sections and the managed workflow,
  and never adds one a project does not have.
- `compagnon init --json` and `compagnon update --json` gain an `integration` array.
- `compagnon doctor [--json] [--strict]` lists what the Compagnon setup still lacks —
  rules, language, skills, specs, decisions, source pins, `CLAUDE.md`, CI,
  pull request template, validation — with the command or skill that fixes
  each item. `compagnon init` and `compagnon status` point to it when something is
  missing, and `/compagnon-onboard` relays its findings.
- The tech lead's "Done when" criteria of the `spec-driven` schema require the
  affected documentation to be updated in a task (or the plan to say none is),
  every spec scenario to be covered by an automated test, and tests to follow
  the project's existing suite, its language's conventions and its `rules`.
  The proposal's Impact names the documentation to update.
- `/compagnon-propose`'s traceability check also requires an automated test per
  scenario and a documentation task when Impact touches documented behavior.
- `/compagnon-apply` writes tests like the project's existing suite, takes the
  test command from the configuration, manifest or CI instead of guessing it,
  and runs the full test suite once before reporting the change as done.
- `/compagnon-configure` proposes testing rules grounded in the project's existing
  tests, falling back on mainstream Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go
  and Java conventions when there are none yet.
- `compagnon changelog` generates release notes from the archived changes — Keep a
  Changelog, plain markdown or JSON — between two git refs, by default since
  the latest `v*` tag, and `--write` keeps a managed `[Unreleased]` section of
  `CHANGELOG.md` up to date; `--release <version>` turns it into a dated
  version block.
- Proposals carry a `## Release note` section, categorized for end users;
  `compagnon validate` warns when an active change has none
  (`release_note_missing`) and rejects an unknown category or an empty item
  (`release_note_invalid`).
- `compagnon doctor` checks that `CHANGELOG.md` matches what `compagnon changelog`
  generates (`changelog`, a warning only).
- `changelog.exclude` in `_compagnon/config.yaml` leaves out archived changes
  already described by hand in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-09-30

### Changed

- **BREAKING:** Compagnon now speaks English throughout — CLI output and help,
  skills, and artifact templates. Template headings are now English
  (`# Proposal:`, `## Why`, `## What Changes`, `## Capabilities`, `## Impact`,
  `## Context`, `## Decisions`, `# Tasks`…). Scripts or tooling that relied on
  French output or headings must be updated; run `compagnon update` to regenerate
  the skills.
- **BREAKING:** `compagnon init --preset` takes `full`, `minimal` or `custom`.
- The minimal preset now installs `propose`, `explore`, `onboard` and
  `configure`, and the full preset includes `configure` (eight workflows).
- Decisions of the project itself are identified as `project/NNNN` in
  qualified ids and in the JSON output.
- The installers print their messages in English. On Windows, `install.ps1`
  now suggests a PATH command that updates only the user `PATH`, instead of
  `setx`, which can truncate it.
- `compagnon decision new` now creates a `proposed` decision, unsealed, so its
  body can be written before it is sealed; accept it with
  `compagnon decision accept`. Pass `--status accepted` to create and seal it at
  once, as before.

### Added

- `compagnon decision accept <ID>` sets a local `proposed` decision to `accepted`
  and seals its body in the same step. It refuses inherited decisions
  (`cannot_accept_inherited`) and decisions that are not `proposed`
  (`decision_not_proposed`).

- Artifact language: a `language:` key in `_compagnon/config.yaml` (an ISO 639
  code such as `en`, `fr` or `pt-BR`) sets the language skills write proposals,
  specs, designs and tasks in. Structural keywords stay in English.
- `compagnon init --language <CODE>` sets it; otherwise it is detected from the
  locale, falling back to `en`. `compagnon instructions --json` exposes it in a
  `language` field.
- Documentation in English and French, published as a website and embedded in
  the binary. `compagnon docs --lang en|fr` selects the language.
- The documentation website follows the Mairistem design system, with a
  landing page, light and dark themes, and a language switch between the
  English and French editions; `compagnon docs` renders in the same style.
- Continuous integration: formatting, lints, tests on Linux, macOS and
  Windows, a minimum Rust version check, validation of Compagnon's own specs, and
  a dependency audit.
- Issue forms for bug reports and feature requests.

### Dependencies

- Updated `dialoguer` to 0.12, `toml` to 1.1, `pulldown-cmark` to 0.13 and
  `sha2` to 0.11, plus minor updates. Existing seals and `compagnon.lock` files
  are read and written exactly as before.

### Fixed

- `compagnon sync` validates the change first and refuses on errors, like
  `compagnon archive`; both now report the stable JSON code `validation_failed`.
- A `RENAMED` delta written with the template's `### Requirement: <name>` form
  is applied instead of being silently ignored, and renaming a requirement
  that does not exist is reported as `rename_source_missing`.
- Renaming and modifying the same requirement in one delta now works.
- A `MODIFIED` merge keeps the blank line before the next requirement.
- Validation reports unexpected headings inside delta sections
  (`delta_unexpected_heading`) and empty delta sections
  (`delta_section_empty`).
- The `subpath` of a git inherited source now also applies to its decisions.
- `compagnon init` counts the generated `config.yaml` among the files it created.
- `compagnon docs --print` no longer prints an error when its output is piped to a
  command that exits early, such as `head`.
- Decisions saved with Windows (CRLF) line endings are parsed, and changing
  their status keeps their sealed body intact.

## [0.3.2] - 2026-09-28

### Fixed

- `compagnon init` and `compagnon status` now recommend `/compagnon-configure` whenever the
  configuration has no `rules:`. A long auto-detected `context:` no longer
  hides the recommendation.

## [0.3.1] - 2026-09-28

### Added

- `/compagnon-configure` skill: analyzes the project (README, contributing guide,
  docs, a sample of the code) and proposes a richer `context:` and
  per-artifact `rules:` for `_compagnon/config.yaml`. It shows a diff and writes
  only after confirmation.
- `compagnon init`, and `compagnon status` when there is no active change, recommend
  `/compagnon-configure` while the configuration is sparse. JSON output is
  unchanged.
- `/compagnon-onboard` recommends `/compagnon-configure` first on a freshly
  initialized project.

### Changed

- `compagnon init` and `compagnon update` install eight workflows by default, adding
  `configure`. Projects that list `workflows:` explicitly are unaffected.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-28

### Added

- Interactive `compagnon init` with environment detection: it reads the project's
  manifests, license, CI setup and MCP servers, asks at most two questions
  (workflows and project context), and writes a `_compagnon/config.yaml` with a
  comment giving the source of each detected value.
- Detection of Jira and Atlassian MCP servers declared in Claude Code's
  configuration files, filled into `mcp.jira_tool`.
- `compagnon init` options `--yes` (`-y`), `--no-detect` and `--preset`. Without a
  terminal on stdin, `--yes` is implied.

### Changed

- `compagnon init` and `compagnon update` install all seven workflows by default —
  propose, explore, onboard, apply, sync, archive, update — instead of three.
  Projects can still restrict the list with `workflows:`.

## [0.2.2] - 2026-09-24

### Added

- A five-minute tutorial covering the whole cycle, from proposal to archive.
- Diagrams of a change's lifecycle, the crate graph and a delta's lifecycle in
  the documentation.

## [0.2.1] - 2026-09-24

### Added

- Standard open-source project files: contributing guide, changelog, code of
  conduct, security policy, and GitHub issue and pull request templates.
- Explicit credit to [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec) in the
  README and the documentation.
- README badges, table of contents and a diagram of the cycle.

### Fixed

- The distribution spec validates again with `compagnon validate --strict`.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-09-24

### Added

- Prebuilt Windows x86_64 binary, and an `install.ps1` script to install it
  without Rust.
- `compagnon docs`: opens the documentation, embedded in the binary, as a
  self-contained HTML page. `--write <PATH>` writes it to a file instead.
- `compagnon completions <SHELL>` for bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell and elvish.

## [0.1.1] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- Release builds for Intel macOS are cross-compiled from Apple Silicon
  runners.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-09-23

### Added

- Initial release: the propose → apply → sync → archive cycle, seven Claude
  Code skills, architecture decisions with sealing, deviations and promotion,
  `compagnon validate --strict`, project-configured MCP integration, and prebuilt
  binaries for macOS and Linux.
